candidate_relations.reason: There is no history of seizures, renal lesions, or other tuberous-sclerosis features, and biopsy instead reveals a localized epithelial neoplasm.
Vitiligo does not create plate-like subepidermal epithelial cords with PAS-positive glycogen-rich cells.
Trichoepithelioma typically shows basaloid follicular structures, unlike the horizontal pale-cell plate connected repeatedly to the epidermis.
The lesions began in adulthood and their biopsy contains a dermal epithelial tumor rather than isolated congenital hypopigmentation.
Idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis lacks the glycogen-rich neoplastic cords and epidermal connections seen histologically.
Seborrheic keratosis would be an epidermal acanthotic lesion, not a plate-like subepidermal tumor with cord-like attachments.
An eccrine poroma forms poroid epithelial lobules and ductal structures, which are not the horizontal clear-cell follicular pattern described.
Pityriasis alba cannot explain persistent alopecic macules containing a true dermal epithelial neoplasm on biopsy.
The symmetric adult-onset facial macules and horizontal pale-cell tumor do not match a typically verrucous congenital epidermal nevus.
The biopsy describes pale glycogenated cords in a plate-like configuration without invasive basaloid nests or malignant features of basal cell carcinoma.
Prior antifungal treatment failed, and histology demonstrates an epithelial tumor rather than yeast or hyphae in the stratum corneum.
A tumor of the follicular infundibulum is an adnexal tumor, but this umbrella term omits its diagnostic epidermally connected pale-cell architecture.
Dermatofibroma has a spindle-cell dermal proliferation rather than PAS-positive epithelial cells arranged in branching cords.
No mature sebaceous lobules surround a central duct; instead the lesion is composed of glycogen-rich clear epithelial cells.
The multiple acquired hypopigmented macules show follicular epithelial tumor histology, not melanocytic nests.
Neither invasive basaloid carcinoma nor trichoepitheliomatous follicular nests matches the characteristic subepidermal plate with multiple epidermal connections.
Extramammary Paget disease would show pagetoid malignant cells within epidermis, absent from this horizontally oriented subepidermal lesion.
Symmetric facial hypopigmented lesions alone do not establish this complex, particularly when biopsy supplies a specific follicular tumor diagnosis.
Degos disease produces porcelain-white atrophic papules with wedge-shaped ischemic histology, not glycogenated epithelial cords.
Syringoma would show small tadpole-shaped ducts in a fibrous stroma rather than a broad plate connected to the overlying epidermis.
